body:
Artificial intelligence in strategic technology

Artificial intelligence (AI) refers to computational methods that enable machines to perform tasks associated with abilities such as recognising patterns, processing language, classifying information and supporting decisions.

In many modern applications, AI models learn patterns from examples rather than relying entirely on instructions written separately for every situation. Their performance depends on the quality of data, the task and the conditions in which the model is used.

AI does not necessarily understand a situation in the same way as a human. A system may produce an incorrect result even when it appears confident.

Civilian and defence applications

AI is a dual-use technology. It can help doctors examine medical images, transport operators identify problems, factories inspect products and disaster-response teams study satellite images.

In defence-related settings, possible applications include:

  • Image analysis: Helping analysts identify patterns in large volumes of aerial or satellite imagery.
  • Predictive maintenance: Using equipment-condition data to estimate whether a machine may require attention.
  • Logistics: Supporting the allocation, tracking and distribution of supplies.
  • Information processing: Assisting trained personnel in reviewing large quantities of data.
  • Simulation and training: Supporting practice, assessment and decision-making exercises.

These applications differ from authorising a machine to make decisions about the use of force. An AI-supported analysis tool can assist human personnel without controlling a weapon.

Automation, remote operation and autonomy

The following terms are related but not interchangeable.

System typeWho or what controls its activity?Example
Remote-controlledA human operator directs the system from elsewhereRemotely piloted inspection drone
AutomatedPredefined rules perform a specified taskEquipment that switches off at a preset temperature
AI-assistedAn AI model analyses information or recommends a resultSoftware highlighting possible defects in an image
AutonomousThe system selects or performs actions within defined operating conditionsRobot navigating around obstacles

A drone is an uncrewed vehicle and is not necessarily autonomous. It may be remotely controlled, programmed for certain movements or equipped with autonomous functions.

Similarly, autonomy does not always require AI. A system may perform a defined task independently using conventional sensors and fixed rules. Conversely, an AI model may support a human without making any independent physical decisions.

Benefits and limitations

AI can help people examine more information and identify patterns that might otherwise be overlooked. It can also produce false results when data are incomplete, unfamiliar, manipulated or unrepresentative.

Common risks include inaccurate classification, biased training data, privacy violations, software vulnerabilities, unclear responsibility and excessive dependence on machine-generated recommendations.

In high-consequence settings, developers and operators need suitable testing, monitoring and human oversight. A model that performs well during development may behave differently when real-world conditions change.

IndiaAI Mission

The Union Cabinet approved the IndiaAI Mission on 7 March 2024, with an outlay of ₹10,371.92 crore over 5 years. Its purposes include strengthening computing infrastructure, datasets, AI innovation, skills, startup support and responsible AI development.

IndiaAI is a cross-sector national AI initiative administered through the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. It should not be confused with iDEX, which specifically supports defence and aerospace innovation.

Prelims focus

  • AI can support image analysis, maintenance, logistics and decision-making.
  • A remotely controlled drone is not necessarily an autonomous drone.
  • Autonomy and AI are related but distinct concepts.
  • IndiaAI Mission was approved on 7 March 2024.
  • The approved IndiaAI Mission outlay was ₹10,371.92 crore over 5 years.
  • Trap: An AI recommendation is not automatically a verified fact or an authorised human decision.

[Sources: Press Information Bureau, Cabinet Approves Ambitious IndiaAI Mission to Strengthen the AI Innovation Ecosystem, 7 March 2024; Press Information Bureau, Government of India Promotes AI and Digital Technology Adoption, 30 July 2026; International Committee of the Red Cross, Frequently Asked Questions: Autonomous Weapon Systems, sections on autonomy and human control. Official and institutional websites consulted 14 November 2026.]

body:
What makes quantum technology different?

Quantum technology uses properties of matter and energy described by quantum physics. At very small scales, particles such as electrons and photons can behave differently from ordinary objects.

Important quantum concepts include superposition, where a quantum system can be described by a combination of possible states, and entanglement, where the measurement results of linked quantum systems show correlations that cannot be explained by treating the systems as completely independent classical objects.

These properties can support new ways of computing, communication and measurement. Their usefulness depends on the task and the maturity of the technology.

Classical bits and quantum bits

Ordinary computers represent information using bits, each with a value of 0 or 1. A qubit, or quantum bit, can exist in a quantum combination of the states associated with 0 and 1 before measurement.

Quantum computers use such quantum states in specialised computations. They may offer major advantages for certain problems, but they are not automatically faster for every task. Building useful systems also requires controlling errors and maintaining delicate quantum states.

Four important branches

Quantum computing

Quantum computing explores how qubits can process information in ways different from ordinary digital computers. Potential applications include selected scientific simulations and computational problems.

Quantum communication

Quantum communication uses quantum properties in information exchange. A well-known application is Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), which can help communicating parties detect certain forms of attempted interception during the establishment of encryption keys.

QKD is not the same as sending all messages through a quantum computer. It also does not make an entire communication network automatically secure against every form of attack.

Quantum sensing and metrology

Sensing means detecting physical changes. Metrology is the science of measurement. Quantum effects can support very precise measurements, including applications involving magnetic fields and timekeeping.

Quantum materials and devices

This field investigates materials and components that display or exploit quantum behaviour. It supports the development of useful quantum technologies rather than referring to a single finished product.

Why quantum technology has strategic importance

Quantum research has potential civilian benefits in computing, scientific instruments, communication and industry. It also has strategic relevance because communication security, accurate measurement and advanced computation can matter to national security.

These are areas of technological potential, not proof that a proposed system is already available for routine military use. In particular, experimental demonstrations and large-scale deployment are different stages of technological maturity.

National Quantum Mission

The Union Cabinet approved the National Quantum Mission (NQM) on 19 April 2023, with an outlay of ₹6,003.65 crore for 8 years, from 2023-24 to 2030-31.

The mission is implemented through the Department of Science and Technology (DST). It seeks to advance quantum research, build technological capabilities, develop skills and support cooperation between research institutions and industry.

Four thematic hubs

AreaLead institutionLocation
Quantum ComputingIndian Institute of ScienceBengaluru
Quantum CommunicationIIT Madras, in association with C-DOTChennai
Quantum Sensing and MetrologyIIT BombayMumbai
Quantum Materials and DevicesIIT DelhiNew Delhi

These thematic hubs coordinate research groups and institutions. The lead institution is not the only organisation participating in the corresponding research field.

Prelims focus

  • A classical bit represents 0 or 1; a qubit is a quantum information unit.
  • Quantum Key Distribution is associated with quantum communication.
  • National Quantum Mission was approved on 19 April 2023.
  • The approved NQM outlay was ₹6,003.65 crore for 2023-24 to 2030-31.
  • NQM is implemented through the Department of Science and Technology.
  • Trap: Quantum computing does not guarantee faster performance for every problem.

[Sources: Department of Science and Technology, Mission Governing Board Finalises Implementation Strategy and Timelines of NQM; DST, Call for Pre-Proposals for Thematic Hubs under National Quantum Mission, January 2024; DST, Key Achievements During 2024, National Quantum Mission and Thematic Hubs; DST, Annual Report 2025-26, Chapter III, National Quantum Mission. Official website consulted 14 November 2026.]

title: Quantum Technology and India's National Quantum Mission

body:
Understanding speed categories

The term Mach number compares the speed of an object with the local speed of sound. Because the speed of sound depends on conditions such as temperature, a given Mach number does not always correspond to exactly the same speed in kilometres per hour.

Supersonic motion is faster than the speed of sound. Hypersonic motion is conventionally described as motion at approximately Mach 5 or above, meaning at least 5 times the local speed of sound.

Hypersonic flight involves scientific challenges associated with very high speed, including significant heating and the need for reliable measurement and control. These observations are sufficient for understanding the basic technology category.

Hypersonic describes a speed regime. It does not by itself identify the vehicle's propulsion method, purpose or exact flight path.

Distinguishing types of high-speed systems

ConceptBasic meaningImportant distinction
Supersonic flightFlight faster than the local speed of soundDoes not necessarily reach Mach 5
Hypersonic flightFlight at approximately Mach 5 or aboveA speed category, not a single vehicle type
Ballistic missileFollows a trajectory that includes a substantial ballistic phaseMay reach hypersonic speed
Hypersonic glide vehicleGlides at hypersonic speed following an initial launch phaseNot identical to a conventional ballistic trajectory
Hypersonic cruise vehicleUses powered flight during a hypersonic cruise phaseDifferent from an unpowered glide vehicle

The categories overlap in important ways. For example, a ballistic missile can move at hypersonic speed during part of its flight. Therefore, a statement that all hypersonic objects are hypersonic cruise vehicles would be incorrect.

Indian research milestones

On 7 September 2020, DRDO reported a successful flight test of its Hypersonic Technology Demonstrator Vehicle (HSTDV), demonstrating aspects of hypersonic air-breathing technology.

On 16 November 2024, DRDO conducted a successful flight trial of an indigenously developed long-range hypersonic missile off the Odisha coast. The Ministry of Defence reported the trial on 17 November 2024.

Both are important research and testing milestones. Neither announcement should automatically be interpreted as proof that every associated technology had entered routine operational service.

What is a directed-energy system?

Directed-energy technology concentrates energy toward a selected object rather than relying on a conventional physical projectile. Two broad forms are:

  • Laser systems: Use concentrated light energy.
  • High-power microwave systems: Use electromagnetic energy in the microwave region.

Such technologies have civilian applications in industry, measurement and research as well as potential defence applications. Their behaviour depends on the energy source, operating environment and target material.

Laser-based systems can be affected by atmospheric conditions and require an appropriate line of sight. Directed-energy systems also depend on sufficient electrical power and suitable safety arrangements.

Laser and microwave systems are both electromagnetic technologies, but they use different regions of the electromagnetic spectrum. Neither should be confused with a conventional gun that propels a physical projectile.

Indian directed-energy development

DRDO reported the first flight tests of an Integrated Air Defence Weapon System conducted on 23 August 2025. The demonstration included a high-power laser-based Directed Energy Weapon along with other air-defence components.

This is a useful illustration of emerging technology being evaluated alongside established defence systems. The announcement concerns a test, and it should not be treated as proof of unrestricted operational deployment.

How to interpret reports of technological success

Reports of research progress frequently use terms such as demonstrated, flight-tested, certified, contracted and inducted. These terms describe different stages. A reliable statement about a project should identify exactly what was announced and when.

Prelims focus

  • Hypersonic speed is conventionally Mach 5 or above.
  • Hypersonic is a speed classification, not a single propulsion technology.
  • DRDO's HSTDV flight demonstration took place on 7 September 2020.
  • DRDO conducted a long-range hypersonic missile flight trial on 16 November 2024.
  • A DRDO air-defence demonstration on 23 August 2025 included laser-based directed-energy technology.
  • Trap: A successful trial does not automatically mean that a system has been inducted into service.

[Sources: NCERT, Science, Class 9, Chapter 8, Motion, section on speed, and Chapter 12, Sound, for foundational physical concepts; Press Information Bureau, DRDO Successfully Flight Tests Hypersonic Technology Demonstrator Vehicle, 7 September 2020; Press Information Bureau, DRDO Carries Out Successful Flight-Trial of India's First Long-Range Hypersonic Missile, 17 November 2024; Press Information Bureau, DRDO Successfully Conducts Maiden Flight-Tests of Integrated Air Defence Weapon System, 24 August 2025. Official websites consulted 14 November 2026.]
